meta.title_plain: How video game graphics draw a whole world 60 times a second
meta.teaser: Triangles, pixels and a super-fast chip: how your games get drawn.

page.title: How your games draw a whole world 60 times a second
page.sub: The science behind video game graphics
page.bigIdea: Every game world is built from tiny triangles. A special chip turns them into colored dots, over and over, faster than you can blink.

cards.title: Everything is made of triangles
cards.front: Your Fortnite skin is secretly a pile of shapes.
cards.back: Game objects are split into tiny flat shapes, usually triangles. Thousands join into a 3D model. Modern graphics chips can handle millions of triangles in every frame.
cards.tryit: Fold a paper strip into triangles and tape them into a pyramid. That's a tiny 3D model!

cards.title: Textures paint the triangles
cards.front: Bare triangles look like grey plastic.
cards.back: A texture is a flat picture wrapped onto the triangles, like a sticker. It adds wood grain, bricks or the pattern on a character's outfit.
cards.tryit: Wrap a gift-paper scrap around a box. The box is the model; the paper is the texture.

cards.title: Lights and shaders add mood
cards.front: Why does a sunset level feel warm?
cards.back: Small programs called shaders work out each spot's color. They check where the lights are and whether a surface sits in shadow.
cards.tryit: Shine a phone flashlight on a ball from different sides. Watch the bright and dark parts move.

cards.title: Triangles become pixels
cards.front: Your screen only shows tiny colored dots.
cards.back: Rasterization finds which pixels each triangle covers and fills them in. A 1080p screen has 1,920 by 1,080 pixels: about 2 million dots.
cards.tryit: Look very closely at a screen with a magnifying glass or phone zoom. Spot the tiny dots.

cards.title: Repeat it 60 times a second
cards.front: One picture isn't a game. You need lots.
cards.back: Each finished picture is a frame. Gamers see 60 frames per second as the minimum for smooth play. A GPU splits the work into many small jobs at once.
cards.tryit: Draw a stick figure moving across 10 sticky notes. Flip them fast to make it move.

words.d: A flat shape with straight sides. Games mostly use triangles.
A picture wrapped onto a 3D model to give it detail.
One tiny colored dot on a screen. Millions make a picture.
How many new pictures appear each second. Higher looks smoother.
A graphics chip that does many small calculations at the same time.

quiz.q: What shape are most game models built from?
quiz.hint: Think of the simplest flat shape with straight sides.
quiz.why: Game objects are split into many small triangles that join into a 3D model.

quiz.hint: Remember the gift-paper and box idea.
quiz.why: A texture is a picture wrapped onto triangles, like a sticker on a box.

quiz.q: Why does a game need many frames every second?
quiz.hint: Think about your flip-book of sticky notes.
quiz.why: Lots of pictures shown quickly trick your eyes into seeing smooth motion.

quiz.q: Why is a GPU so fast at graphics?
opts: It does many small jobs at once
quiz.hint: Is it better to have one worker or a whole team?
quiz.why: A GPU splits the picture into tiny pieces and works on them in parallel.

page.think: Next time you play Fortnite or Roblox, which part of the scene would need the most triangles: a tree, a wall or a character? Why do you think so?
